moments.name: We have seen this before: the motor

copy.title: We have seen this before
copy.s1: Around 1900, factories bolted electric motors onto the old line shaft.
copy.s2: The big gains came decades later, when they redesigned the floor around the motor.
copy.s3: The gains came from redesigning the work around the motor, not from adding the motor.
copy.source: Paul A. David, “The Dynamo and the Computer,” American Economic Review, 1990

moments.visual: Full-screen 3D: an old factory with one long rotating line shaft, belts dropping to every machine, all coupled. A motor attaches to the shaft (bolt-on). Then the shaft dissolves, each machine gets its own small motor, and the floor re-flows into a clean line. Warm industrial light → clean modern light.
